python3 - << 'EOF'
import re, os, subprocess

base = "."
roots = ["drivers", "net", "kernel", "fs", "mm", "block", "ipc", "lib", "security", "sound", "crypto", "virt"]

# 1) find tasklet callback registrations and NAPI poll registrations
tasklet_regs = []   # (file, callback)
napi_regs = []      # (file, callback)

pat_tasklet = re.compile(r'tasklet(?:_hi)?_schedule\s*\(\s*&?[^,]*,?\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\)')
pat_tasklet_setup = re.compile(r'tasklet_setup\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\)')
pat_tasklet_init = re.compile(r'tasklet_init\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,')
pat_napi_add = re.compile(r'netif_napi_add(?:_weight|_dev)?\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,')

found = {}
for root in roots:
    for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(os.path.join(base, root)):
        for f in files:
            if not f.endswith(".c"): continue
            p = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
            try:
                src = open(p, errors="replace").read()
            except: continue
            for m in pat_tasklet_setup.finditer(src):
                tasklet_regs.append((p, m.group(1)))
            for m in pat_tasklet_init.finditer(src):
                tasklet_regs.append((p, m.group(1)))
            for m in pat_napi_add.finditer(src):
                napi_regs.append((p, m.group(1)))

print("tasklet callbacks:", len(tasklet_regs))
print("napi polls:", len(napi_regs))

# 2) extract function bodies (brace matching) for the callbacks and check for plain spin_lock
def get_body(src, name):
    # find definition: name( ... ) {  possibly with return type on preceding text
    for m in re.finditer(r'\b' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*\(', src):
        # walk to matching close paren
        i = m.end()
        depth = 1
        while depth > 0 and i < len(src):
            if src[i] == '(': depth += 1
            elif src[i] == ')': depth -= 1
            i += 1
        # skip whitespace/newlines
        j = i
        while j < len(src) and src[j] in ' \t\r\n': j += 1
        if j < len(src) and src[j] == '{':
            # match braces
            k = j; depth = 0
            while k < len(src):
                if src[k] == '{': depth += 1
                elif src[k] == '}':
                    depth -= 1
                    if depth == 0: break
                k += 1
            return (src[:m.start()].count('\n')+1, src[j:k+1])
    return None

def get_line(src, substr):
    idx = src.find(substr)
    return src[:idx].count('\n')+1 if idx >= 0 else -1

plain_lock = re.compile(r'spin_lock\s*\(')
bh_lock = re.compile(r'spin_lock_(?:bh|irqsave|irq|irqrestore)\s*\(|local_bh_disable|local_irq_disable|local_irq_save')

for label, regs in (("TASKLET", tasklet_regs), ("NAPI", napi_regs)):
    print("=== %s callbacks with plain spin_lock in body ===" % label)
    for p, name in regs:
        try:
            src = open(p, errors="replace").read()
        except: continue
        b = get_body(src, name)
        if not b: continue
        body = b[1]
        if plain_lock.search(body) and not bh_lock.search(body):
            print("%s:%s def-line~%d" % (p, name, b[0]))
EOF

Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()

    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Excellent context. Now I understand the pattern well. The intent i040 is branch3 = tasklet-napi-softirq-lock for snapshot s11. I need to find locks shared between process-context code (workers, ioctls, open/close, config, firmware request handlers) and code executing in TASKLET or NET softirq context (tasklet_schedule/tasklet_hi_schedule callback bodies, NAPI poll functions reached via napi_schedule, or other NET_RX/NET_TX softirq callbacks), where process-context takes plain spin_lock() instead of spin_lock_bh().

Exclusions: xmit-callback and timer-callback paths (covered by branches 1-2). Also exclude the ks7010 seed.

Interesting notes from previous artifacts for s11:
- mwl8k: stream_lock reported under xmit-branch; tx_lock correctly disciplined (tasklet mwl8k_tx_poll at 4642 uses plain spin_lock in softirq context — that's the softirq side, process side uses _bh, so safe).
- wil6210: net_queue_lock — plain site in NAPI TX poll softirq context; xmit uses _bh. Safe for xmit branch. But wait — for tasklet/NAPI branch: is there any process-context plain caller of net_queue_lock? The i012 artifact said "no process-context plain caller of this lock was found." So safe.
- wil6210 txdata->lock: plain in wil_is_tx_idle (suspend, process context) vs wil_tx_ring (xmit softirq) — that was branch1 (xmit). The xmit path is excluded from my branch. But actually wil_tx_ring is reached from wil_start_xmit (ndo_start_xmit) which is xmit-softirq — excluded (branch 1, already noted unresolved in i012). Hmm, but if txdata->lock is also taken in NAPI poll (TX completion) contexts... Actually wil_tx_complete is NAPI poll context. import re, subprocess, json, sys

ROOT = "/mnt/raid/home/yangning_placeholder"
ROOT = "/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s11"

# candidate (file, lockexpr) pairs from tasklet & napi scans
softirq_sides = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
out = {}
for f, entries in softirq_sides.items():
    rel = f[len(ROOT)+1:]
    src = open(f, errors="replace").read()
    # map lock expr -> all spin_lock-like sites
    locknames = {}
    for e in entries:
        for ln, expr in e.get("plain_locks", []):
            locknames.setdefault(expr, set()).add(e.get("callback") or e.get("poll"))
    for expr, cbs in locknames.items():
        # extract lock base name from &a->b.c
        base = expr.lstrip('&').split('->')[-1].split('.')[-1].strip()
        # find all acquisitions in file
        sites = []
        for m in re.finditer(r'(spin_lock(?:_bh|_irqsave|_irq|_save)?)(?:_lock)?\s*\(\s*([^;()]+?)\s*[,)]', src):
            if base in m.group(2):
                line = src[:m.start()].count('\n')+1
                sites.append((line, m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()))
        out.setdefault(rel, []).append({"lock": expr, "base": base, "softirq_cbs": sorted(cbs), "sites": sites})

print(json.dumps(out, indent=1))

Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.

    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)

    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)

    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

content.thinking:
Huge list. This is a kernel snapshot (probably ~5.10). I need a strategy to narrow down.

Key insight: For a tasklet or NAPI-based driver, the typical bug pattern:
- Driver has an IRQ handler that does tasklet_schedule() or napi_schedule()
- The tasklet callback or NAPI poll function takes lock X with spin_lock
- Some process-context path (workqueue worker, ioctl, open/close, config, firmware load) takes lock X with plain spin_lock
- => deadlock

A quick approach: for each file with tasklet usage, check what locks the tasklet callback takes, and whether the same locks are taken with plain spin_lock elsewhere.

Actually, let me think of well-known real bugs of this class:
- ks7010 (seed)
- rtl8188eu / rtl8192u staging
- wlan-ng
- hostap
- cw1200
- p54pci
- ipw2100/ipw2200
- b43legacy
- orinoco
- at76c50x-usb
- carl9170

Given previous branch searches found mwl8k in s11 for xmit branch, and timer branch found something (f018). Let me check what i026 found for s11 in timer branch — to avoid duplicating a finding.

Actually the instructions say branches are distinct: exclude xmit-callback and timer-callback paths. So I should focus on:
1. tasklet callback bodies taking spin_lock, shared with process-context plain spin_lock of the same lock.
2. NAPI poll functions taking spin_lock (plain), shared with process-context plain spin_lock.

Let me write a script approach. For each candidate file:
1. Find tasklet callback function name (DECLARE_TASKLET / tasklet_init with function arg).

    src = open(f, errors='replace').read()

    names = set()
    for m in re.finditer(r'tasklet_init\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*,', src):

    for m in re.finditer(r'tasklet_setup\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\)', src):

    for m in re.finditer(r'DECLARE_TASKLET(_OLD)?\s*\(\s*[^,]+,\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)', src):

import re, os

# For each tasklet callback function, check whether its body contains a plain spin_lock
lines = open(W+'/tasklet_callbacks.txt').read().splitlines()
plain_pat = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock\s*\(')
hits=[]
for ln in lines:
    path, names = ln.split(' :: ')
    f = S + '/' + path
    try:
        src = open(f, errors='replace').read()
    except: continue
    src_lines = src.splitlines()
    for name in names.split(','):
        # find function definition
        # match: name(...) { ... }  - find start
        mdef = None
        for i,l in enumerate(src_lines):
            if re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_].*\b'+re.escape(name)+r'\s*\(', l) and not l.strip().startswith('*') and not l.strip().startswith('//'):
                # crude: definition line like "static void name(...)"
                if re.search(r'\b'+re.escape(name)+r'\s*\([^;]*$', l):
                    mdef = i; break
        if mdef is None: continue
        # capture body until brace balance closes
        depth=0; started=False; body=[]
        for i in range(mdef, min(mdef+400, len(src_lines))):
            l = src_lines[i]
            body.append((i+1,l))
            depth += l.count('{') - l.count('}')
            if '{' in l: started=True
            if started and depth<=0:
                break
        bodytext = '\n'.join(l for _,l in body)
        if plain_pat.search(bodytext):
            hits.append((path, name, mdef+1))
print(len(hits))
with open(W+'/tasklet_plainlocks.txt','w') as fh:
    for p,n,l in hits:
        fh.write(f'{p} :: {n} :: defline {l}\n')
for p,n,l in hits: print(p,n,l)
EOF

tasklet_hits = [l.split(' :: ') for l in open(W+'/tasklet_plainlocks.txt').read().splitlines()]

print('tasklet plain-lock callbacks:', len(tasklet_hits), ' napi files:', len(napi_files))
# NAPI poll functions: netif_napi_add(..., fn, ...)
napi_polls = {}
for f in napi_files:
    src = open(f, errors='replace').read()
    names=set()
    for m in re.finditer(r'netif_napi_add(?:_exclusive|_weight)?\s*\(\s*[^;]*?', src):
        pass
    for m in re.finditer(r'netif_napi_add\s*\(([^;]*?)\)\s*;', src, re.S):
        args = m.group(1)
        # find function name: typically 2nd or 3rd arg; take identifier that's a function-looking name
        ids = re.findall(r'([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*(?:,\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*)*$', args.strip())
        # simpler: last identifier-ish arg before weight number
        parts = [p.strip() for p in args.split(',')]
        # find candidates: args that look like fn and are not & and not NAPI_POLL_WEIGHT
        for p in parts:
            p2 = p.strip().lstrip('&')
            if re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*', p2) and p2 not in ('NAPI_POLL_WEIGHT','NAPI_NO_POLL',):
                # heuristic: pick the one that ends with 'poll' or is 2nd/3rd arg
                if 'poll' in p2.lower():
                    names.add(p2)
    if names:
        napi_polls[f]=names
print('files with named poll fns:', len(napi_polls))
with open(W+'/napi_polls.txt','w') as fh:
    for f,names in sorted(napi_polls.items()):
        fh.write(f.replace(S+'/','')+' :: '+','.join(sorted(names))+'\n')
for f,names in sorted(napi_polls.items()):
    print(f.replace(S+'/',''), '::', ','.join(sorted(names)))
EOF

plain_pat = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock\s*\(')
def get_body(src_lines, name, maxscan=600):
    mdef=None
    for i,l in enumerate(src_lines):
        if re.search(r'\b'+re.escape(name)+r'\s*\(', l) and re.search(r'\b'+re.escape(name)+r'\s*\([^;]*$', l):
            # exclude calls with ; on same line quickly
            mdef=i; break
    if mdef is None: return None
    depth=0; started=False; body=[]
    for i in range(mdef, min(mdef+maxscan, len(src_lines))):
        l=src_lines[i]; body.append((i+1,l))
        depth += l.count('{')-l.count('}')
        if '{' in l: started=True
        if started and depth<=0: break
    return body

Important subtlety: spin_lock_irqsave on fep->lock happens BEFORE spin_lock(&fep->tx_lock) in close. Does local_irq_save() prevent softirq? Yes — local_irq_save disables local interrupts, and softirqs only run with interrupts enabled (softirq processing happens on irq exit or ksoftirqd). While IRQs are disabled, no softirq can preempt.                 if ';' in lines[k]:

                k += 1
            if started:

                    if depth == 0 and '{' in ''.join(lines[k:k2+1]):
